psychic-wave.descripcion: A wave of psychic energy ripples through the room, violently prying into the minds of creatures in the area and alerting Kemnebi to the presence of intruders.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 50 (legendary) to stymie the psychic energy before it manifests

shadow-hooks.descripcion: Hooks of solidified shadow extend from the walls, hook into creatures, and pull, tearing them open.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 50 (legendary) to disable the trap's sensors

visage-of-asmodeus.descripcion: A looming illusory image of the face of Asmodeus appears within the room, eyes glinting with malice at any who refuse to worship him.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 50 (master) to disrupt the rune projecting Asmodeus's face or Religion DC 48 (master) to refute the Asmodean faith; four total successes are required to disable the hazard
datos.rutina:
(1 action; mental, visual) The illusory face of Asmodeus gazes at one creature in the area who doesn't worship Asmodeus. His eyes glint with diabolic power as that creature is overwhelmed by visions of the enormity of Hell. That creature must attempt a Will DC 44 saving throw. The hazard tends to target creatures who are attempting to disable the hazard. Taking damage from this hazard doesn't grant a flat check to end the Confused condition.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature takes 5d8 mental damage.
Failure The creature takes 10d8 mental damage and is confused for 1 round.
Critical Failure The creature takes 20d8 mental damage and is confused for 1 minute.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates 1 round after all creatures who don't worship Asmodeus either leave the room or are dead. It resets 1 round after that.

wave-of-damned-souls.descripcion: A torrent of souls pulled from Hell pours through an archway, inflicting their personal suffering on all they touch.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 50 (master) or Religion DC 50 (master) to quell the souls' suffering; these checks must be attempted while adjacent to the arch, and four total successes are required to disable the haunt
datos.rutina:
(1 action; divine, void) A seemingly endless flow of damned spirits emerges from the arch and washes down the street. Each creature within a 240-foot line from the arch down the street takes 4d10+24 void damage with a Fortitude DC 44 save. This line affects everyone within 20 feet of the ground.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature takes half damage.
Failure The creature takes full damage and increases its doomed value by 1.
Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and increases its doomed value by 2.
datos.reinicio: After 1 minute, the wave of souls dries up, and the haunt deactivates. Over the course of 1 hour, planar energy rebuilds in the area, and the haunt resets.

avernal-vortex.descripcion: The edges of the extraplanar tunnel seem to writhe with malevolence, as if preventing unwanted souls from passing through.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 50 (master) or Religion DC 50 (master) to allow the group to traverse along the portal tunnel; six total successes are required to complete the journey; a PC who succeeds at a Acrobatics DC 48, Athletics DC 48, or Survival DC 48 check as a 2-action activity grants themselves a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against the hazard's routine for 1 round (on a critical success, they can also grant this bonus to one other PC)
datos.rutina:
(1 action; divine) The Avernal vortex churns across the portal tunnel, stopping the PCs from reaching their ultimate destination. In the first round, the vortex takes an action to attempt to dispel all beneficial spells on all creatures in the tunnel, scouring them with Hellfire. The vortex has a counteract modifier of +43 and a counteract rank of 10, and rolls separately for each spell. On a success, the target creature takes 4d6 fire damage with a basic Fortitude DC 45 save (this has the divine, fire, and unholy traits).
In the second round, the vortex attempts to instill a dread of tumbling forever through the tunnel to those within it; each creature takes 6d6 persistent damage with a basic Will DC 45 save (this is an emotion and mental effect). Once a creature ends its persistent mental damage (or if they avoided the persistent damage), they can reach and escape the tunnel.
In all subsequent rounds, the vortex releases bolts of acid, cold, fire, and electricity. It makes one vortex bolt Strike against each creature in the tunnel.
datos.reinicio: Once the PCs pass through the portal tunnel and arrive in Hell, the Avernal vortex ends and doesn't reset.

earthfall.descripcion:
Variant Megatsunami and Meteor Shower
Anticipate Astronomy-lore DC 42 (master) or Nature DC 45 (legendary) to chart the meteor's trajectory, Society DC 50 (master) to recall information on Xin-Bakrakhan and how it was destroyed during Earthfall
Prepare Ocean-lore DC 42 (expert) or Nature DC 45 (master) or Survival DC 45 (master) to chart the flood paths of the coming waves, Crafting DC 50 (legendary) to reinforce a shelter

datos.rutina:
(5 minutes) Only the first five minutes of this disaster directly impact the PCs, but during that time, they must contend with the combination of a megatsunami and meteor shower.
Meteor Shower: As Meteor Shower, but 7d10 bludgeoning damage and 15d6 fire damage to all characters (basic Reflex DC 42 save). If at least half the PCs succeeded at Prepare checks, only one randomly determined PC is affected by the meteor shower rather than the whole party.
Tsunami: If at least half the PCs succeed on Prepare checks, they avoid all effects of the megatsunami until the last minute, at which point they're affected as if they were unprepared. Many of Xin-Bakrakhan's citizens are powerful wizards or otherwise have access to flight, be it by spell, wings, or flying minions, but their retreat into the skies above is chaotic. A PC capable of flight (or who is carried aloft by a flying ally) for an entire minute can avoid the tsunami's effects if they succeed at a Acrobatics DC 35 check to Maneuver in Flight to avoid mid-air collisions with others or falling meteors—on a failure they're forced back into the dangerous waters below and take a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against the tsunami's effects.
The tsunami floods into the lowest elevation area on the 2nd minute, then proceeds up into the higher regions as shown on the map on each of the following minutes. A PC in the area is affected as the standard megatsunami, but 6d12+35 bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude DC 42 save) when they're first struck and then 4d12+25 bludgeoning damage (basic Reflex DC 40) each minute they're carried along by the wave.

gorging-passage.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
gorging-passage.descripcion: The passage closes around intruders. Cavities open in its soft wood and try to envelope anything within it.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 50 (legendary) three times to scrape away Hidden sensors on the floor and walls, or Nature DC 55 (legendary) to call upon lingering elements of primal energy in the Witchbole to render the trap inert
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The trap's first action on its turn is to heave and jolt, causing the entire length of area E4 to become difficult terrain until the start of the gorging passage's next turn. It then grinds at those within while simultaneously exuding acid from its walls. All creatures in area E4 take 4d10 bludgeoning,8d6 acid damage (basic Reflex DC 45 save).
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates as soon as a round begins with no living targets in area E4, and then resets at the start of the following round.

malfunctioning-perfumery-eastern.descripcion: The magically and mechanically automated tools Sorshen used to aid in the crafting of perfume on the long, eastern workbench have interacted in unexpected ways, transforming the workshop into a dangerous peril.

datos.desactivar: Crafting DC 52 (legendary) to quickly introduce neutralizing agents into the alchemical machinery, Thievery DC 55 (master) to disable the mechanized portions of the devices, or Arcana DC 55 (master) to counteract magical elements; four total successes are required to disable the hazard (destroying one of the four workbenches counts as one success)
datos.rutina:
(5 actions) On its initiative, the malfunctioning perfumery takes the following five actions, in order. For each success at disabling it, the hazard loses one action. The targets for actions 2–5 are randomly chosen from creatures in the room, with no one creature being targeted more than once before all other creatures in the room have been targeted. For example, a party of 4 PCs will each be targeted by one of these actions. If just a single PC is in the room, they will be targeted by all four.
• 1: Crushing Notes 1 (olfactory, poison) The malfunctioning machinery exudes a blast of concentrated and overwhelming perfume notes into area B11. Creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude DC 45 save or become Stunned 1 (Stunned 2 on a critical failure).

• 2: Nozzle Spray 1 (poison) Nozzles built into the machinery extend out to spray toxic, overwhelmingly cloying perfume in multiple directions. One randomly determined target in area B11 takes 14d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 45 save).

• 3: Sillage 1 (emotion, mental) A larger, more intimidating nozzle than the one utilized in the previous action extends forward and violently sprays a staggering array of different scents at a random target in the room. The overwhelming mixture of lingering scent (the perfume's sillage) causes the creature to take 10d6 mental damage (basic Will DC 45 save); on a failed save, the creature is also Slowed 1 for 1 round by the overwhelming scents.

• 4: Oil Spill 1 (fire) Sparks from grinding machinery ignite a patch of spilled oil somewhere in the room—a random creature in area B11 takes 10d6 fire,4d6 persistent damage (basic Fortitude DC 45 save).

• 5: Boiling Beaker 1 (emotion, mental) A pressurized beaker containing boiling fluids springs a leak, and a dislodged tube sprays disorienting, psychotropic fumes at a random creature in the room, who must then succeed at a Will DC 44 save to avoid becoming Confused for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure).

queen-sorshen-s-aid.descripcion: Queen Sorshen is a beautiful Thassilonian woman wielding a shimmering guisarme. Her violet eyes are fierce and focused, but the corner of her lips twist up in a small, lopsided smile.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 55 to unravel the energies allowing Sorshen to continue to vex Xanderghul; 4 successes are required to disable the hazard.
datos.rutina:
(3 actions) On her initiative each round, Sorshen can spend her three actions on any of the following options, following PC suggestions if requested. She cannot use any action from the following list more than once per round.

—
Aid Ally 1 Sorshen uses her magic to empower one of the PCs, granting that PC a +4 circumstance bonus to attack rolls until the start of her next turn. Effect: Queen Sorshen's Aid (Aid Ally)

—
Dispel Pride 1 Sorshen attempts to counteract a magic effect put in place by Xanderghul, with a counteract rank of 9th and a {+40} modifier for the roll.

—
Distracting Presence 1 Sorshen uses her power to distract Xanderghul, causing him to lose his resistance to mental damage until the start of her next turn and also to attempt a Will DC 50 save with the following results.
Critical Success Xanderghul takes no further penalty, and is temporarily immune to Distracting Presence for 24 hours.
Success Xanderghul is Off-Guard until the start of his turn.
Failure Xanderghul is off-guard until the start of Sorshen's next turn.
Critical Failure As failure, but Xanderghul is also Slowed 1 as long as he remains off-guard.

—
Indulgent Arcana 1 Sorshen empowers a PC's magic, so that the next spell with the mental trait they cast before Sorshen's next turn increases its save DC and attack roll by 2 and removes the spell's incapacitation trait, if any. Effect: Queen Sorshen's Aid (Indulgent Arcana)

—
Sinuous Strike 1 Sorshen swings her guisarme, usurping some of Xanderghul's own power to manifest an illusory duplicate that attempts a guisarme Strike against him.

twist-of-fate.descripcion: Seldeg's ritual nears its conclusion, causing magical energy to arc erratically between the ritual circles.

datos.desactivar: Arazni-lore DC 44 or Iomedae-lore DC 44 to recount a tale from history that grounds that deity in the current reality, Crafting DC 50 (legendary) to create a device to siphon energy from the ritual circle, or Religion DC 46 (legendary) to discharge the escalating divine energy; six successes (three successes per circle) are required to disarm the hazard.
datos.rutina:
(1 action; divine) The divine energy gathered by the ritual spikes. One of the eleven stained-glass windows (each depicting one of her Eleven Acts) transforms to feature Arazni instead. Any creature that can see the window change must attempt a Will DC 50 save.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is immune to this effect for 10 minutes.
Success The creature is unaffected.
Failure The creature takes 3d12+20 mental damage.
Critical Failure The creature takes 6d12+40 mental damage. If the creatures' next d20 roll is a critical success, they earn a critical failure instead. This is a misfortune effect. If all 11 windows transform, Seldeg's ritual finishes ahead of schedule. The stained-glass windows shatter, dealing 8d10+52 piercing damage (Reflex DC 50 save) to each creature in the room. The hazard then becomes inactive.
datos.reinicio: While atop the floating platform, Seldeg Bhedlis can use a 3-action activity with the auditory trait to reenergize the ritual. Doing so removes one success to disable the hazard and immediately triggers the hazard's Reorder Reality reaction.
